reviews.review: This has great art style, snappy skill based gameplay with RNG perks, weapons, and upgrades, the perfect cup of tea.

TLDR: Core game is solid, however future acts need to mix it up and use its already solid mechanics in a cool, interesting, and new way.
Guns feel good, movement feels VERY good, and music sounds good. So many things go together very well that this game easily becomes addicting but RQ only has 3 levels so far.
The issues so far range from lack of content (early access which makes sense) and some general game mechanics being alright.
7/8 out of 10

—-
Good mix of roguelite and arena/boomer shooter. This will fall more in the reigns of doom eternal type boomer shooter. You feel fast not due to base movement speed but the overall mechanics you juggle from weapon swapping, class specific skills, and strong movement. More of a juggernaut running through a bunch of enemies type feel of Doom instead of an untouchable hit/run type feel like ultrakill. Very few flawed elements that pulls the project down but a lot of alright elements though.

[b][u]Pros: [/u][/b]
+++ [b]Gameplay.[/b]
	+ Promotes Aggressive Play. Map Design, XP system, and slow enemy fire all promotes aggressive play
	+ Gunplay + Weapon Depth and how it works with other game mechanics. Auto-reloading is an amazing mechanic which keeps you on the move all the time. Mix it with alt fires, weapon specific things, and elements creates a lot of depth.
	+ Movement. At first I thought base movement was very slow. You can't fire when sprinting. HOWEVER, you can slide+jump for ALOT of movement which adds so much depth to both movement and gameplay

+++ [b]Maps.[/b] So far all maps look unique and distinct. Interesting "Linear Arena format". Basically jumping from one mini arena and the next section is also a mini arena.
	+ Movement feels good in these maps. Never felt "overly" overwhelmed with enemy placement / projectiles.

+++ [b]Replay.[/b] Muti pathways, Muti classes, Muti weapons on top of a very solid foundation leads to a lot of replayability.

+++ [b]Music.[/b] Pretty good and surprising amount of variety. Works well thematically.

[b][u]Meh:[/u][/b]
||| [b]Classes.[/b] Pretty standard classes: Tank/Stealth/Turrets/Solder. 
	| Usually the perks/level up adds diversity in the kits but these are pretty standard that we have seen in other games before. 
	| Workable but not nothing new

||| [b]Aesthetics.[/b] Overall not bad. Graphics are stylized pretty well. Guns, effects, etc all fit pretty well.
	| Some visuals need updating. (main character girl in 2D vs 3D)
	| Enemy design works but nothing really standouts / starts looking the same despite technically being different.

||| [b]Story.[/b] Workable but still early access.
	| NGL i didn't pay much attention. There is some good visual storytelling in the maps and the comic book animations post level are interesting but not going to make a major statement on this until full release

||| [b]Enemies.[/b] A lot of good but could use some other work
	| Every level RQ brings in new enemy types from basic tiny projectile enemies to flying robots shooting horizontal projectiles.
	| There are a lot of enemies that require different movements to counter however they all die exactly the same. Just shoot them enough. No weak points, no using stuff against them, enemy friendly fire, etc.
	| Late game "fatigue". Plus despite different projectiles, the models are (generally) the same and all feel the same. Act 3 feels sluggish, not due to the level design/goliaths but due to how everything feels the same.

||| [b]Weapons.[/b] Some bloat however good core and high potential.
	| ALOT of good weapons but some weapons feel the same. Esp in the red weapons / Rapid fire weapons. Red category need stronger identity
	| Technically all weapons have some form of difference (ex Red LM VS Red+Yellow minigun) but some just feel redundant (ex Uzi vs Assault SMG / Sawoff vs Pump). 
	| I do enjoy the RNG stats and such. Those are cool

||| [b]Perks / Upgrades[/b]
	| Overall i tend to either 1) pick the option with the same color as my weapon 2) Only focus on the stat and ignore the color. Probably should be changed to fix this.
	| I liked the play-test system but that needs more tweaking.

[b][u]Cons:[/u][/b]
--- [b]Early Access.[/b] Not done therefore not all content. Not deducting any points but still need to consider when buying

---  [b]Homebase[/b]
	- Not anything that interesting. Not much storytelling, layout is meh, etc 
	- Hub for upgrades but only like 4 interactable stations while you can upgrade a bunch.

---  [b]Currency / Weapon Upgrades[/b](in both homebase and ingame)
	- Never been a fan ongoing currency you can use for both ingame weapons/upgrades and out game upgrades.
	- Outgame upgrades feel a bit incremental and a lot of times you don't feel the change / feel stronger. 
	- Ingame upgrades feel a bit weird b/c i feel you should be strong due to your weapons + build + skill that you got but the wrench upgrades feels "pay to win"   


[b][u]Nitpicks / Possible issues:[/u][/b]
- XP Pickup. I do like the XP game mechanic b/c it promotes aggressive play however you don't always want to play close range or even mid range. The most interesting part I experienced was I was super aggressive but was getting A rank in XP. This was b/c I was TOO aggressive where I would kill 1 enemy then go to another. B/c I was focused on the fighting, I didn't pick up the XP which is counter to the aggressive play.
- Late-Late game Scaling. In games like Risk of Rain 2, end game you are a god, being able to clear floors. You tend to lack this in RQ which may affect the power dynamic of Rougelites. something to consider.
- Red Weapons. Not sure if the color system will stay ( based on current play-test) but might as well mention it. Need stronger identity. Maybe guarantee an alt fire. Maybe good against specific things.
- Great 2D art VS meh 3D art. Main girl 3D model should be updated to look more in line with the rest of the art. 
- Enemies. Better visual identity for enemies. All look same-y and in late game feels same-y. Maybe specific types of armor. Maybe future maps with have pathing to these types of enemies. You as a player have to decide based on your build which path to take.

[b][u]Recommendations.[/u][/b] I aint no game designer but a few ideas
- Hub Upgrade VS specific incremental updates. Overall hub upgrade would feels more powerful and create a distinct form of progression. With the current system, i focused a lot on more material upgrades such as classes/perks/etc. I filled up the other smaller upgrades (afflixes, rng , etc) last.
- Quick Swap Weapons. Flare gun is my favorite weapon and bow is my fav second weapon. Flaregun adds new depth to the weapon gameplay loop. Debuffing / combo weapons are dope and add to the aggro style.
- Auto-Reload notification. Some for of notification when your side arm is done reloading would be nice
- Arenas. Having bigger well crafted arenas in the maps will prevent the player from being bored from the “linear mini arenas” format.

[b][u]Final words:[/u][/b]
Overall pretty good. Closest thing we will get to a “Arena shooter Roguelite” done well. The very strong foundation, such as combat, handling, and movement, allows great moments and futureproofing. When you are in-game you can feel the amount of care and thought put in so many of the foundational systems.
At this point RQ should focus on bumping up the workable / alright systems, such as the hub, perks, and currency, in a way that works with the foundation. Def worth it.
